The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "The New Testament in Modern Hebrew, translated by Salkinson and Ginsberg
Public Domain
Language: עברית (Hebrew)"

Why this is public domain:
Translators: Isaac Edward Salkinson (born 1820 in Vilna, died 5 June 1883 in Vienna) and Christian David Ginsburg (born 25 December 1831 in Warsaw, died 7 March 1914 in Palmers Green, England). The New Testament was published posthumously under Ginsburg's supervision in Vienna in 1886.
United States: first published in 1886, before 1931, so public domain in the United States.
Country of origin (Austria, where it was published): life plus 70 years. Salkinson's term ended at the end of 1953, so the text is public domain there from 1954. Ginsburg's term ended at the end of 1984, which is also before 2026 under the United Kingdom's life plus 70 rule, his country.

Sources of these facts:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Salkinson (dates and the 1886 Vienna publication)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_David_Ginsburg (dates)
https://ebible.org/hebsg/copyright.htm (statement and title)
https://ebible.org/details.php?id=hebsg (translators, file name hebsg1886eb)

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-hebsg-ec75e0d5, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
